title: Herdr port: lines param, send_text, PaneScroller strategies
action: Per D2/D3/D4/D5/D9/D10 (round 5 — same mechanism, fixes only a missing revision field found in round 4 review, no other change): change Herdr::read_pane to take explicit `lines: usize` AND `source: ReadSource` arguments, where ReadSource is a new small enum (Visible, Recent) added to src/herdr/mod.rs matching herdr's own source vocabulary. `lines` is ignored by herdr when source is Visible, still required for Recent. Update ALL THREE implementors to compile: SocketHerdr (send the real `source` value instead of hardcoding "recent" — src/herdr/socket.rs:466; lines capped at herdr's own 1000 for Recent), FakeHerdr, and the test-only RecordingHerdr stub in src/web/create.rs:323-337. Also update the ONE production call site, src/web/screen.rs:27, to pass ReadSource::Recent + lines: 80 (herdr's own existing default, named explicitly) — compile-fix only, no new endpoint logic (that's cell 2). Add Herdr::send_text(&self, pane_id: &str, bytes: &str) -> Result<()> implemented on SocketHerdr (calls herdr's pane.send_text raw-byte channel, per D5 — never send_keys/send_input) and FakeHerdr. Extend FakeHerdr with a history-aware per-pane shape: a longer stored history string sliceable by the requested `lines` for ReadSource::Recent, plus a separate fixed slice for ReadSource::Visible. Add a new PaneScroller port in its own file src/herdr/pane_scroller.rs (struct or trait wrapping &dyn Herdr) with read_history(pane_id: &str) -> Result<ScreenRead> (reusing the existing ScreenRead{text, revision} wire type from src/herdr/wire.rs — NOT a bare Vec<String> or String — so cell 2 can build ScreenBody from it directly, matching the existing non-history response shape) implementing this mechanism (no capacity gate): (1) read source: Visible; (2) read source: Recent with lines: 1000 [NativeScrollback]; (3) if the Recent read is strictly richer than the Visible read, return the Recent ScreenRead as-is (its own revision carried through); (4) OTHERWISE (Recent not richer than Visible, covers exact equality and any unexpected non-richer case identically) escalate [EscapeInjection]: send_text raw PageUp (\x1b[5~), re-read Visible (this becomes the returned ScreenRead, its revision carried through), ALWAYS send_text raw Ctrl+End (\x1b[1;5F) afterward to restore the live bottom regardless of what the escalated read returned. The strategy-selection code (step 3/4's branch) must carry a WHY-comment (D10) explaining: alt-screen VT100/xterm semantics never retain scrollback (D1); selection compares actual read results, never scroll.max_offset_from_bottom or the pane's agent name (D3); and escalating once for a short primary-screen pane is an ASSUMED-harmless no-op (not independently verified against a real shell pane — only Claude Code/alt-screen was live-tested with these bytes), recorded as an accepted risk in plan.md's Risk Map, not asserted as settled.

truths: Herdr::read_pane's source parameter actually changes SocketHerdr's request body (source: visible or recent), not hardcoded to recent
Herdr::read_pane's lines parameter is honored for ReadSource::Recent, capped at herdr's own 1000; ignored for ReadSource::Visible

SocketHerdr, FakeHerdr, and RecordingHerdr (src/web/create.rs) all compile against the new read_pane signature; src/web/screen.rs's existing call site is updated to pass ReadSource::Recent with lines: 80 (unchanged from today's actual default)
Herdr::send_text sends raw bytes via herdr's pane.send_text channel, never send_keys or send_input
PaneScroller::read_history returns a ScreenRead (text + revision), reusing src/herdr/wire.rs's existing type, never a bare Vec<String> or String with no revision
PaneScroller::read_history returns the Recent(1000) ScreenRead when it is strictly richer than the Visible read, without ever calling send_text in that case
PaneScroller::read_history escalates to EscapeInjection whenever Recent(1000) is not richer than Visible, and always sends a restore-to-bottom Ctrl+End via send_text after any EscapeInjection read

FakeHerdr's extended per-pane shape lets a unit test construct all three cases: short pane (escalates, returns the harmless result with its own revision), primary-screen pane with real extra history (NativeScrollback), alt-screen pane (EscapeInjection)
prohibitions: Do not use Herdr::send_keys or Herdr::send_input for the escape sequences — D5 requires send_text specifically
Do not branch strategy selection on scroll.max_offset_from_bottom or the pane's agent field — D3 requires comparing actual read results
Do not add an at-capacity/viewport-dimension gate before escalating — round 3 explicitly drops this
Do not return read_history's result as a bare Vec<String>/String with no revision — cell 2 needs a revision value
